candidate.answerReason: Substituting x=1 and x=-1 gives y₁=a+b+c and y₂=a-b+c. Their difference is 2b=-6, so b=-3.

methods.label: Subtract the values at opposite inputs
methods.explanation:
At \(x=1\) and \(x=-1\), the squared terms agree. Subtracting the corresponding function values will therefore cancel the terms involving \(a\) and \(c\). Substitution gives
\[
y_1=a+b+c,\qquad y_2=a-b+c.
\]
Consequently,
\[
-6=y_1-y_2
=(a+b+c)-(a-b+c)=2b.
\]
Dividing by \(2\) yields \(b=-3\), choice A.
